assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational, wide-ranging account of how political institutions, incentives, state capacity and fiscal choices jointly shape economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: The proposed laureates represent central complementary contributions to modern political economics, though the broader literature is extensive.
assessment.maturity: The research program is long established, influential across economics and adjacent social sciences, and well suited to retrospective recognition.
uncertainties: The breadth of the contribution makes a tightly bounded three-person attribution difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data have transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and made the geography and mechanisms of unequal opportunity empirically tractable.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are closely identified with the program and its major empirical advances.
assessment.maturity: The body of work has accumulated over more than a decade and has reshaped both research and public-policy debate.
uncertainties: The precise division between a prize for measurement and one for substantive causal conclusions remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction of long-run income and wealth distributions has fundamentally changed the empirical basis for studying inequality and taxation.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman are leading architects of the linked historical and administrative-data research program.
assessment.maturity: Its datasets, methods and findings have had sustained international influence and permit substantial scholarly assessment.
uncertainties: Some measurement choices and interpretations of offshore wealth and wealth concentration remain actively debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs provided unusually direct evidence on discrimination and set a durable standard for field-based measurement of unequal treatment.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are especially strongly associated with landmark audit-study contributions; credit extends beyond any single study.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated, adapted across settings and incorporated into a mature evidence base.
uncertainties: External validity and the interpretation of callback outcomes as broader labor-market discrimination require care.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework supplied a powerful quantitative lens for relating firm-level distortions to productivity and large cross-country income gaps.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia made central complementary contributions to the measurement and quantitative interpretation of misallocation.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and has generated a large subsequent literature testing and extending its implications.
uncertainties: Mapping observed dispersion into policy-relevant distortions rests on consequential modeling assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work made trade and technology shocks central to an empirically grounded understanding of changing local labor markets and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are closely associated with the leading empirical framework; Katz is also an important contributor to the wider agenda.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been intensively studied, replicated and extended, with lasting influence on labor and trade research.
uncertainties: Separating trade, technology and other concurrent local shocks remains empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The economic treatment of exhaustible natural assets, biodiversity and inclusive wealth broadened the framework for evaluating sustainable prosperity.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are central figures in connecting intertemporal welfare analysis with natural-capital constraints.
assessment.maturity: The intellectual contribution is longstanding and its relevance has increased as environmental constraints have become more economically salient.
uncertainties: Valuing biodiversity and translating inclusive-wealth concepts into operational measures remain challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of risk sharing, informal insurance and village economies brought rigorous theory and evidence to central development constraints.
assessment.attribution: Townsend, Udry and Rosenzweig made major, complementary contributions to this research program.
assessment.maturity: The work has long informed development economics and has stimulated extensive theoretical and empirical follow-on research.
uncertainties: Evidence from particular village settings may not transfer straightforwardly to all institutional environments.
